facts.statement: Planohybodus is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the family Hybodontidae.
facts.quote: Planohybodus (from Latin planus, "flat", and "Hybodus") is an extinct genus of hybodont

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Middle Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous across Europe and the Indian subcontinent.
facts.quote: known from the Middle Jurassic-Early Cretaceous (Bathonian-Barremian) of Europe (including Great Britain, France, Spain, Switzerland, Poland, and possibly Denmark) and the Indian subcontinent

facts.statement: Fossils of Planohybodus have been discovered in both marine and freshwater environments.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in marine as well as freshwater environments

facts.statement: A tooth of Planohybodus was found embedded in an ammonite shell, indicating it could attack hard-shelled prey.
facts.quote: A specimen of the ammonite genus Orthaspidoceras from the Late Jurassic of France has been found with an embedded tooth of Planohybodus

facts.statement: The genus Planohybodus was described by Rees and Underwood in 2008.
Planohybodus belongs to the subfamily Hybodontinae.
Planohybodus is classified within the family Hybodontidae.
Planohybodus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Planohybodus lived between 168.2 and 83.6 million years ago, from the Bathonian to the Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Santonian (168.2 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Planohybodus peterboroughensis is estimated to have grown to lengths of 2 to 3 meters.
facts.quote: Planohybodus peterboroughensis is suggested to have reached lengths of 2-3 m

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Planohybodus is Planohybodus peterboroughensis.
Planohybodus grossiconus is a species found in England, Scotland, France, and Russia during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Planohybodus grossiconus (Agassiz, 1843) England, Scotland, France, Russia, Middle Jurassic (Bathonian)

facts.statement: Planohybodus ensis is a species found in England and Spain during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Planohybodus ensis (Woodward, 1916) England, Spain, Early Cretaceous (Berriasian-Barremian)

facts.statement: Records of Planohybodus from Mexico, Brazil, and North America are currently unconfirmed.
facts.quote: Possible records have been reported from the Late Jurassic of Mexico, the Early Cretaceous of Brazil (Planohybodus marki) and the Late Cretaceous (Santonian) of North America, but these are unconfirmed

rejected.statement: The status of Planohybodus marki is uncertain, indicated by a question mark in its classification.
